title: Keep Your Cut Fresh: Practical Tips from 3D Cutz in Norwich
description: Practical tips from 3D Cutz, Norwich to keep your haircut looking sharp for longer — styling, products, gentle trims and daily care.

content.heading: Choose a cut that grows out well
paragraphs: Some styles hide regrowth better than others. If you want to stretch the time between visits, ask for a cut with slightly longer length on top and a soft, blended taper at the back and sides — textured layers tend to sit better as they grow.
Before you leave the chair, ask 3D Cutz to show you how the shape will look after a few weeks so you can pick a style that suits your routine and hair type.

content.heading: Use the right products and apply them correctly
paragraphs: A little product goes a long way. For most short styles, a small amount of matte paste or clay gives texture and control without weighing hair down; lighter creams work well for thicker hair and salt sprays help fine hair keep volume.

Apply styling product to towel-dried hair and work from roots to ends, finishing with a quick blast from a hairdryer if you want extra hold. Avoid piling on product — that’s what makes hair go greasy and limp between washes.

content.heading: Simple upkeep you can do at home
paragraphs: Keep the edges neat to preserve a fresh look: use a personal trimmer with a guard for the neckline or learn a simple neckline tidy-up your barber can demonstrate. If you’re not confident with tools, a quick visit for a tidy-up is friendlier than risking a heavy-handed DIY job.
Comb or brush daily to keep the shape and remove product build-up; a soft toothbrush works well for short, close-cut areas around the ears and hairline.

content.heading: Treat your hair and scalp well
paragraphs: Washing frequency depends on your hair and lifestyle. If your hair gets oily, wash with a gentle shampoo every other day and condition sparingly on the ends. Over-washing strips natural oils and can make hair look flat and dry.

Small habits make a difference: sleep on a cotton or silk pillowcase to reduce friction, rinse out chlorine or salt after swimming, and keep hydrated — a healthy scalp supports a neater-looking cut for longer.
